jessica (support): FYI customer tk-948 hitting 400 schema validation on tool call. They say py/ts/go clients behave differently when passing a labeled arg that contains a null byte (\u0000).

mike (eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact error and the raw request body from each client?

jessica (support): From the customer: "400 Bad Request - schema: 'metadata' must be string without NULL chars". They attached two samples — TS and Python. Trimming sensitive bits.

jessica (support): TS client outgoing body (snippet):
```json
{"model":"x-small","input":{"tool_call":{"name":"index_doc","args":{"content":"file:\u0000end","metadata":"title\u0000v1"}}}}
```

jessica (support): Python client outgoing body (snippet):
```python
{"model":"x-small","input":{"tool_call":{"name":"index_doc","args":{"content":"file:\\x00end","metadata":"title\\x00v1"}}}}
```

priya (py-sdk): that python snippet looks fine — Python sends a raw null byte (\x00) inside the JSON string which is technically invalid JSON, but our serializer escapes it as \u0000. We do `json.dumps(s)` which becomes `\\u0000` in network payload.

oliver (ts-sdk): Hmm. TS `JSON.stringify` also escapes null as `\u0000`. But we had a bug in our tool-call layer where labeled args get `Buffer.from(value).toString('base64')` for binary detection, then wrapped again if content-type inference flagged it. Could be double-encoding for certain labeled keys.

mike (eng-runtime): If one client sends literal `\\u0000` and the other sends base64 for the same field, runtime schema validation (we run a strict unicode check) will reject base64-looking strings in some routes. Can you capture the raw HTTP payload as received by the API gateway?

alex (sre): Captured ingress for TS request (raw bytes, hex):
```
7b 22 6d 6f 64 65 6c 22 3a 22 78 2d 73 6d 61 6c 6c 22 2c 22 69 6e 70 75 74 22 3a 7b 22 74 6f 6f 6c 5f 63 61 6c 6c 22 3a 7b 22 6e 61 6d 65 22 3a 22 69 6e 64 65 78 5f 64 6f 63 22 2c 22 61 72 67 73 22 3a 7b 22 63 6f 6e 74 65 6e 74 22 3a 22 66 69 6c 65 3a 4e 55 4c 4c 42 41 53 45 36 34 22 2c 22 6d 65 74 61 64 61 74 61 22 3a 22 7469746c65 5f 62 33 61312222 7d 7d 7d
```
(Note: we replaced long blobs for readability). The ingress hex shows `BASE64` marker for the content field in TS path.

priya (py-sdk): Customer also attached their python http dump — it shows `\u0000` escape sequences in the JSON body (no base64 marker).

oliver (ts-sdk): Repro locally: TS SDK treats any arg with `\u0000` as binary and base64-encodes it, but then our tool-call marshaller wraps all labeled args again into a JSON string which causes the runtime to see something unexpected. That matches the `schema validation` error.

mike (eng-runtime): Okay. Two issues: 1) runtime rejects certain encoded forms for labeled string fields when they look like base64 tags; 2) TS SDK double-treatment changes semantics. We should triage both.

jessica (support): Customer asks for workaround — they can’t change input (ingesting raw OCR with occasional nulls). Any short-term mitigations?

oliver (ts-sdk): Quick workaround: set `sdkConfig.force_string_for_tool_args = true` or disable the binary-detection flag in the TS client so it never base64-encodes those fields. I'll add docs.

priya (py-sdk): For Python customers, we already `escape_unicode=True` so `\u0000` reaches the server. No change needed.

mike (eng-runtime): We'll add tolerant parsing on the runtime that accepts either `\u0000` escapes or base64-wrapped content for labeled args, but we need a clear signal to avoid turning every string into binary. Eng/Runtime will own the compatibility fix; TS-SDK will ship a patch to stop auto-base64ing labeled args unless explicitly marked binary.

alex (sre): Marking incident P2 for now. If customer sees large traffic impact we'll escalate. :eyes:

support-bot: Created ticket INF-1427 and linked customer tk-948. Assigned to eng-runtime + ts-sdk.

mike (eng-runtime): Action items:
- oliver: PR to TS SDK to disable binary-detection for labeled tool args (small patch).
- runtime: accept `\\u0000` and base64 variants for string-labeled args for next minor.
- support: pass workaround flag to customer.

jessica (support): Thanks — I've sent workaround and ticket ID to the customer. Will update when they confirm it's working. :thumbsup:
